decisions.statement: The property's own page is written whole at the path handed in.
The property's page type and slug are read from that path.
A path naming no page type a page property is is refused.
A path already holding a body is refused rather than written over.
A body exporting no object is refused.
The key each page gains is the one that body states under `property-slug`.
A body stating no `property-slug` is refused.
The property is named after the parts the one page handed in for that already names.
The declaration goes into the `properties` of every page type handed in.
A declaration holding many values states a count, and that count is nothing.
A declaration holding one value states the default handed in.
A default is spelled as text on the declaration and as its own kind on a page.
What the property's values hold is read from the page type its own page is.
A default that kind cannot hold is refused.
A declaration holding many values is refused a default.
The key is put on every page of those page types, holding that default.
A page of a page type beneath a declaring page type gains the key too.
Which pages gain the key is read from the values the index files for each type.
No page body is read to find out which pages gain the key.
No page gains the key where the caller states no default.
The key is written last on every page, since no page writes it yet.
A call naming no page type is refused, since nothing would declare the property.
A path naming no page type is refused.
A page stating that key already is refused by its path.
One body is read once however many passages it gains.
The passages of one body land as one answer over that body.
No file a page type generates beside the property's page is written here.
Nothing here gives the page its `id`.
Nothing here reaches a change.

definition: one page property made, with its page, its part, every declaration of it and every page's key
